body.statement: For every \(T\subseteq\mathcal V\) and ordering \(t\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\), the construction in \(\text{def:positive-noise-completion}\) yields a model in \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\) with target set \(T\), covariance \(\operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)=\Sigma_e\) for all \(e\in\mathcal E\), strictly positive baseline structural-noise variances, and strictly positive stationary measurement-error variances.
body.justification: A covariance certificate is causally meaningful only if every certified label set has a legal SCM witness with positive noise.
body.gap: Yang et al. begin from a separately recovered mixing matrix, and measurement-error identification begins from separability; neither proves arbitrary-baseline realization from covariance shifts alone.
body.consumer: The construction lets an applied analyst interpret every reported target set as a realizable alternative causal explanation rather than an algebraic artifact.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(T\) and an ordering \(t\) for which \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\) holds.  Put \(W=W_t\), \(L=L_t\), \(D=D_t\), and \(A=W L\).  The certificate and the definitions give
\[
 P_tA=P_tQP_t^{\mathsf T}Q_{tt}^{-1}L=L,
 \qquad
 P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}=L\Lambda_{e,t}L^{\mathsf T}. \tag{2}
\]
Apply \(\text{lem:range-reconstruction}\) first to \(N=Q\) and then to \(N=\Delta_e\), using the exact-rank and common-range assumptions.  Since \(Q_{tt}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), equation (2) yields
\[
 Q=WQ_{tt}W^{\mathsf T}=ADA^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \Delta_e=W(P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T})W^{\mathsf T}
 =A\Lambda_{e,t}A^{\mathsf T}. \tag{3}
\]
In particular, all \(\Delta_e\) are positive semidefinite because each \(\Lambda_{e,t}\) is diagonal and entrywise nonnegative.  For \(e=1\), uniqueness in (2) gives \(\Lambda_{1,t}=D\): indeed both are diagonal and
\(L\Lambda_{1,t}L^{\mathsf T}=Q_{tt}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), so multiplication by \(L^{-1}\) and \(L^{-\mathsf T}\) gives equality.

Permute the observed coordinates so that the ordered labels \(t_1,\ldots,t_r\) occur first.  Write \(A_{T^c}\) for the remaining rows of \(A\), and define
\[
 U=\begin{pmatrix}L&0\\ A_{T^c}&I_{d-r}\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This matrix is unit lower triangular, is invertible, and its first \(r\) columns are exactly \(A\), by (2).  The inverse of a unit lower triangular matrix is unit lower triangular: solving \(UX=I_d\) successively by rows gives diagonal entries one and entries above the diagonal zero.  Therefore \(B=I_d-U^{-1}\) is strictly lower triangular in this permutation and is an acyclic observed structural matrix.  Undoing the permutation preserves the original labels and proves the required permutation-similar acyclicity.

Let \(a_0=\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_0)>0\), whose positivity is \(\text{ass:baseline-positive}\), and choose \(\tau\) as in \(\text{def:positive-noise-completion}\).  For every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 x^{\mathsf T}R_0x
 =x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_0x-\tau\lVert U^{\mathsf T}x\rVert_2^2-\tau\lVert x\rVert_2^2
 \ge \bigl(a_0-\tau(\lVert U\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2+1)\bigr)\lVert x\rVert_2^2
 >\frac{a_0}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2. \tag{4}
\]
Thus \(R_0\succ0\).  Diagonalizing this real symmetric matrix as \(R_0=O\operatorname{diag}(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_d)O^{\mathsf T}\), with \(O\) orthogonal and every \(\rho_j>0\), defines the positive square root
\(R_0^{1/2}=O\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\rho_1},\ldots,\sqrt{\rho_d})O^{\mathsf T}\).

For each environment take mutually independent vectors
\[
 H_e\sim N(0,I_d),\qquad
 \eta_e\sim N(0,\tau I_d),\qquad
 \varepsilon_e\sim N\!\left(0,\tau I_d+\operatorname{diag}_t(\Lambda_{e,t})\right), \tag{5}
\]
where \(\operatorname{diag}_t(\Lambda_{e,t})\) places the diagonal entries of \(\Lambda_{e,t}\) on the labels \(t\), places zero elsewhere, and \(\Lambda_{0,t}=0\).  Also set \(C=U^{-1}R_0^{1/2}\).  Equation (5) explicitly supplies centered Gaussian primitives and the mutual independence required by \(\text{def:legal-scm-class}\).  Their latent covariance \(I_d\), loading \(C\), and measurement covariance \(\tau I_d\succ0\) are invariant over environments.  The baseline structural variance vector is \(\tau\mathbf 1_d>0\); increments vanish off \(T\), are nonnegative on \(T\), and the reference entries are the strictly positive diagonal entries of \(D\).  Hence the changing set has exactly the declared \(r\) labels \(T\).

At the baseline, independence and the definition of \(Y_e\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_0)
 =UCC^{\mathsf T}U^{\mathsf T}+\tau UU^{\mathsf T}+\tau I_d
 =R_0+\tau UU^{\mathsf T}+\tau I_d=\Sigma_0. \tag{6}
\]
At environment \(e\), only the structural covariance in (5) changes.  Since the corresponding columns of \(U\) equal \(A\), (3) and (6) imply
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)-\operatorname{Cov}(Y_0)
 =A\Lambda_{e,t}A^{\mathsf T}=\Delta_e,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(Y_e)=\Sigma_0+\Delta_e=\Sigma_e. \tag{7}
\]
All member conditions of \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\), including strict structural and measurement-noise positivity, have now been checked from the construction, and (7) proves the asserted covariance realization.
